What to pick up next

Each line is one ingredient you don't have yet, with the Recipe Book dishes it would let you cook.

Best fuses from your bag

Each row is the best material in your bag for that job. Weapon totals add the material's fuse power to the weapon's own attack. Tap a name for where to find it.

Weapons

Arrows

Fuse a material to an arrow from the bow's arrow menu; it's used up with the arrow.

Shields

Weapons, bows and shields

Every one you can fuse to, with its own attack (guard for shields), durability and trait, and the best fuse for it from your bag. "Decayed" is the gloom-worn version found around Hyrule; "pristine" is the unworn one.

What each material does when fused

Fuse power is the attack it adds to a weapon. On an arrow, teeth, claws, talons, nails and hooves count double. Zonai devices and the objects at the end can't go in your pouch: fuse them where you find them.

Fuse effects

What a fused material can add besides attack, and which materials do it.

Forge

Pick a weapon, bow or shield and what to fuse to it, to see what you get.

Builds and blueprints

Community favorites with parts and steps, Switch 2 designs to load by QR code, and all 46 Autobuild schematics. Save a build to keep it, or tap Surprise me.

Drawings are this page's own sketches; each guide has the real photos and video.

What each device does, whether it needs battery power, where its capsules come from, and the builds here that use it.

Everyday places. Nothing hidden: secrets have their own tab.

Secrets map

All recipes

Numbered as in the in-game Recipe Book. "Needs" uses the game's own recipe rules; effects list what each dish can carry and an ingredient that gives it.

All ingredients

Hearts are per piece. Cooking doubles an ingredient's hearts; ★ is the effect strength it adds to a dish.

Effects and how they scale

Mixing ingredients with two different effects cancels both. Every ingredient adds 0:30 to a timed effect; ingredients with the effect add more, and the total caps at 30:00.

Cooking pot

Pick up to 5 ingredients to see exactly what comes out. Tap a filled slot to take it back out.

Picker won't open?

Some apps can't open your gallery from a page like this. Open this page in Chrome instead (copy its link into Chrome's address bar). Or copy a screenshot, then press and hold in the box below and tap Paste.

Move or back up your bag

Each copy of this app keeps its own bag: this page in Claude, and the app installed on your phone. To move your bag, copy its code here and paste it into the other copy. A saved code is also a backup.

    About this app and its sources

    Recipe rules, ingredient values and the cooking math come from game data extracted by the Tears of the Kingdom datamining community, as published in Echocolat's TOTK Cooking Calculator (built on KingFoo's simulator). This page's cooking engine was checked against that calculator on 5,401 ingredient combinations with zero differences, except that in 429 of them this page's sell price is 1 rupee higher: it multiplies in 32-bit floats like the game's own code (as Breath of the Wild's decompiled cooking code shows), where the calculator uses 64-bit math. It has not been checked in the game itself.

    Shop advisor: armor upgrade costs from the community trackers by Respheal and SturmB, with disagreements settled by the Zelda Dungeon and Zelda Wiki armor pages; sell prices and fuse attack from the same datamined game tables; selling advice from the player guides linked on the Sell tab.

    Recipe Book numbering and the roasting, boiling and freezing methods follow the Zelda Dungeon wiki.

    Fusing, building and map sources are named on their own tabs and in each popup.

    Fan-made reference, not affiliated with Nintendo. All drawings and the painted map are this page's own.
